approvalRequirements: Apply through the state, tribal, territorial, or local LIHEAP administering agency serving the household; the federal office does not approve individual applications.
Meet the administering agency’s current household-income, residency, energy-burden, and other categorical eligibility rules.
Provide the household, identity, income, residence, utility-account, energy-cost, crisis, and other documentation requested by the local agency.
For weatherization or minor energy-related home repairs, reside in a jurisdiction whose current LIHEAP plan offers that benefit and obtain agency approval for the proposed work.
Receive the agency’s eligibility determination and benefit authorization while the applicable allocation remains available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: LIHEAP is a federally funded but locally administered block-grant program with jurisdiction-specific benefits, prioritization, and finite allocations; meeting federal income guidance does not guarantee a weatherization or repair benefit.
reviews.evidenceText: ACF states that households apply through state, tribal, territorial, or local agencies and that LIHEAP may support energy bills, crises, weatherization, and minor energy-related repairs. Eligibility, benefit design, priorities, and available funds are set by each grantee.

approvalRequirements: Own and occupy an eligible Delaware residence and qualify through either the low-income Weatherization Assistance Program pathway or the moderate-income approved-solar-contractor pathway.
Complete the program’s income-verification process, including the requested tax-return or income-release documentation.
Pass the applicable property, roof, site, electrical, and solar-project suitability review.
Use the program-designated agency or an approved solar contractor and receive program approval before installation.
Complete permitting, utility interconnection, installation, inspection, and final documentation required for the approved photovoltaic system.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current Delaware program uses defined income pathways and project-review rules rather than competitive scoring. A qualifying applicant whose site and project are approved is likely to receive the stated solar assistance, subject to program capacity and completion requirements.
reviews.evidenceText: DNREC currently offers separate low-income and moderate-income solar pathways with income verification, site review, approved delivery partners, and preinstallation approval. The current benefit is for solar photovoltaic systems, not an air-sealing or weatherization award.

approvalRequirements: Own, acquire, or develop an eligible Connecticut affordable multifamily or condominium property with at least five dwelling units.
Demonstrate that at least 60 percent of the units satisfy the program’s affordability requirement for households at or below 80 percent of area median income.
Propose eligible energy-efficiency, clean-energy, health, safety, or related property improvements supported by an acceptable scope and budget.
Submit the property, ownership, operating, affordability, project, contractor, cost, and financial documents requested by Capital for Change.
Pass borrower and property underwriting, including repayment-capacity, security, title, and other credit review, and execute the approved loan documents before funding.
Complete the approved work and provide invoices, inspections, certifications, and other disbursement or closeout records.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: LIME is financing rather than an entitlement incentive. A qualifying affordable multifamily project still depends on borrower-specific credit, property, security, project, and repayment underwriting before closing.
reviews.evidenceText: Capital for Change describes LIME financing for qualifying Connecticut multifamily properties with at least five units and a required affordable-unit share. Approval requires a project application and lender underwriting before loan closing and disbursement.

approvalRequirements: Be a Lower Valley Energy residential member and install the measure at an eligible service address.
Select a measure currently offered through the residential conservation program and meet its equipment, efficiency, installation, and replacement specifications.
Obtain any measure-specific energy audit, contractor qualification, preinspection, or written preapproval required before purchase or installation.
Submit the current application with the paid invoice, manufacturer and model information, efficiency records, contractor details, and other measure-specific documents within the filing period.
Allow Lower Valley Energy to inspect or otherwise verify the installation and remain within applicable rebate caps and available program funds.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Lower Valley Energy’s current residential conservation offers are prescriptive and use customer, technical, documentation, and verification rules rather than competitive selection. A complete qualifying claim is likely to be approved, subject to measure limits and funding.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Lower Valley Energy residential conservation page and linked measure materials describe customer eligibility, qualifying equipment and envelope measures, measure-specific preapproval or assessment steps, documentation, and verification.

approvalRequirements: Be a Lumbee River EMC member and satisfy the membership requirements for ElecTel Cooperative Federal Credit Union.
Own an eligible residential property in the cooperative’s service area and use the financing for a currently eligible energy-efficiency improvement.
Submit the loan application and requested borrower, property, contractor, equipment, project-scope, and cost information.
Pass the credit union’s credit, income, repayment-capacity, and other underwriting review.
Execute the loan and repayment documents before funding and use the proceeds only for the approved project.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The program provides member financing through a credit union, so an eligible HVAC or weatherization project is not assured funding until the borrower passes credit underwriting and accepts the loan terms.
reviews.evidenceText: Lumbee River EMC directs members to ElecTel for energy-efficiency loans covering qualifying HVAC, insulation, weatherization, windows, doors, and water-heating work. Approval requires credit-union membership, a loan application, and borrower underwriting.

approvalRequirements: Be a Lumbee River EMC residential member and install the measure at the qualifying service address.
Purchase and install a measure included in the current rebate program and meet the applicable equipment, efficiency, sizing, contractor, and installation specifications.
Use the current measure-specific rebate form and obtain any required preapproval, assessment, testing, or permit before completing the work.
Submit the application with paid invoices, equipment model and rating information, contractor records, photographs, test results, or other required supporting documents by the stated deadline.
Permit Lumbee River EMC to verify or inspect the completed installation before issuing the rebate.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Lumbee River EMC publishes prescriptive residential rebate forms for current measures. A member claim meeting the technical, documentation, timing, and verification rules is likely to be paid after review.
reviews.evidenceText: The current rebate page lists residential forms for heating and cooling, windows, weatherization, heat-pump water heaters, smart thermostats, and other measures and requires measure-specific applications and supporting installation records.

approvalRequirements: Maintain an eligible Madison Gas and Electric residential electric account and an eligible electric vehicle or charging configuration supported by the program.
Enroll in Charge Ahead, connect the required vehicle or charging-platform account, and accept the managed-charging and data-sharing terms.
Keep the enrolled vehicle or charging equipment connected and available for managed charging during applicable events, subject to the program’s operating rules.
Remain on an eligible MGE rate and maintain active enrollment and account standing for each reward period.
Allow MGE or its platform provider to verify charging participation before applying the recurring bill reward or time-of-use savings.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Charge Ahead is a noncompetitive managed-charging program with published enrollment and participation conditions. An eligible customer who remains enrolled and participates is likely to receive the applicable recurring reward or rate savings.
reviews.evidenceText: MGE’s current Charge Ahead page describes managed charging, enrollment, vehicle or platform connectivity, and recurring bill rewards for eligible standard-rate participants. It expressly states that installation of a charging station is not required, so the record’s charger-installation mapping is unsupported.

approvalRequirements: Own and occupy a qualifying residence served under an eligible MGE residential rate and maintain the electric account in good standing.
Submit the home, account, vehicle, parking, electrical-service, and preferred charger-location information required for MGE’s site qualification.
Allow MGE to determine the installation location, electrical scope, equipment, and any customer-paid excess installation cost.
Execute the Home Electric Vehicle Charging service agreement, including the minimum service term, daily service charge, access, equipment-use, and termination provisions.
Maintain compatible wireless internet and the required charging-platform account and permit managed charging and data collection.
Provide MGE and its contractors access for installation, inspection, maintenance, repair, replacement, and removal of the utility-owned charger.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: MGE’s home-charging service uses objective customer, site, contract, connectivity, and payment requirements rather than competitive selection. A qualified homeowner who accepts the service agreement is likely to receive the utility-owned Level 2 installation.
reviews.evidenceText: The current MGE service agreement covers utility installation and maintenance of a networked Level 2 charger at a qualified residence, eligible residential rates, site approval, a minimum service term, a daily charge, customer responsibility for excess installation cost, internet connectivity, and managed-charging participation.

approvalRequirements: Qualify for one of the currently active Maine HEAR delivery pathways: eligible new affordable multifamily housing or an eligible income-qualified single-wide mobile home.
Meet the pathway’s income, property, unit-count, occupancy, existing-heating, and other project eligibility rules.
Submit the required project or household information and receive Efficiency Maine review, preapproval, and an incentive reservation or agreement before installation.
Use a participating contractor and install the pathway-approved qualifying heat-pump, electrical, or related electrification measures.
Complete permitting, installation, testing, final invoices, certifications, and any required quality-assurance inspection before payment.
Complete the approved project while the applicable federal and program allocation remains available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The active HEAR pathways use defined income, property, technical, preapproval, contractor, and verification rules. A project that receives a reservation or incentive agreement and completes the approved work is likely to be paid, subject to available federal funds.
reviews.evidenceText: Efficiency Maine currently limits HEAR delivery to defined affordable-multifamily and single-wide-mobile-home pathways with income or affordability tests, preapproval, approved installation, final documentation, and quality assurance. The current public pathways do not support a general industrial process-electrification award.

approvalRequirements: Respond to an active Maine NEVI or related public fast-charging solicitation rather than submitting a general customer rebate claim.
Propose a site that meets the solicitation’s geographic priorities and document site control, utility service, permitting, schedule, community access, and operational commitments.
Provide the required technical design, eligible-cost budget, nonfederal match, financial capacity, team qualifications, and implementation plan.
Meet current federal NEVI requirements for charging power, port count, public access, reliability, payment, interoperability, operations, maintenance, cybersecurity, and reporting.
Receive competitive evaluation, selection, contract execution, environmental and federal compliance approval, and authorization before reimbursable work begins.
Complete construction, commissioning, reporting, and reimbursement documentation under the awarded agreement.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Maine deploys NEVI funding through periodic competitive solicitations, and the current official opportunities page did not show an open general NEVI fast-charging solicitation at the audit date. An unselected general applicant is therefore unlikely to receive an award.
reviews.evidenceText: Efficiency Maine describes public charging support through competitive opportunities and reports that a recent NEVI phase was awarded in March 2026. As of July 10, 2026, no open general NEVI direct-current fast-charging solicitation was verified on the current opportunities page.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible residential customer in participating Oregon utility territory and complete the current income-qualification process.
Use the applicable Energy Trust consumer-owned solar or income-qualified battery pathway and a participating trade ally or other approved delivery channel.
Select a qualifying battery system that meets current minimum capacity, equipment, solar-pairing, installation, and interconnection specifications.
Submit the project through the current PowerClerk or program workflow and obtain an incentive reservation before installation.
Complete permitting, installation, commissioning, utility interconnection, and final invoice, equipment, and income documentation before the reservation expires.
Complete the project while the applicable utility allocation and incentive step remains available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Energy Trust’s current income-qualified battery offering uses published eligibility, reservation, technical, and closeout conditions and processes applications as received. A reserved qualifying project is likely to receive the incentive while its utility allocation remains available.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Energy Trust materials list income-qualified battery incentives, income-eligibility forms, PowerClerk project processing, Equitable Solar resources, step-based allocations, and reservation requirements. The legacy Making Solar Equitable title now leads into these current equity-focused solar and storage resources.

approvalRequirements: Be a Mansfield Municipal Electric Department residential customer and install the measure at the qualifying service address.
Purchase and install a measure included in the current 2026 rebate portfolio and meet its technical, efficiency, sizing, contractor, and installation specifications.
Complete any required home energy assessment, connected-device enrollment, preapproval, permit, testing, or preinstallation verification for the measure.
Submit the correct 2026 application with the paid invoice, product model and serial number, efficiency documentation, contractor information, and other required attachments.
File the completed claim by the published deadline and permit MMED or its program administrator to inspect or verify the installation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: MMED publishes current 2026 prescriptive rebate forms and objective claim rules. A qualifying customer who follows the measure-specific process and files complete documentation by January 31, 2027 is likely to receive the rebate.
reviews.evidenceText: MMED’s current page identifies 2026 appliance, heat-pump, weatherization, electric-vehicle, connected-device, and assessment offerings and states that 2026 rebate forms must be postmarked by January 31, 2027.

approvalRequirements: Be a Marblehead Municipal Light Department residential customer and install the measure at the eligible service address.
Use a measure currently offered by MMLD or NextZero and meet its equipment, efficiency, installation, contractor, and customer eligibility requirements.
Complete any required no-cost energy audit, preapproval, connected-device enrollment, testing, or other measure-specific step before installation.
Submit the current application with paid invoices, manufacturer and model information, efficiency ratings, contractor records, and any other required supporting documents.
Allow MMLD or its program administrator to verify the installation and comply with current filing deadlines, caps, and funding limits.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: MMLD and NextZero currently publish residential energy-assessment and rebate pathways with objective customer, product, documentation, and verification rules. A complete claim for a currently listed measure is likely to be approved, subject to measure limits and funds.
reviews.evidenceText: MMLD’s current rebate page directs customers to NextZero and provides current appliance, home-energy, heat-pump, connected-home, and assessment resources. Some retrofit categories in the source record are broader than the measures specifically documented on the current official pages.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Marietta Power or Marietta Water residential customer for the claimed measure and install it at the qualifying account address.
Select a measure currently listed by the city and meet its product, conversion, efficiency, flow-rate, installation, and customer-account specifications.
Obtain preinstallation verification or written approval when the city identifies it as required for the measure.
Submit the rebate application with dated paid receipts, product and model information, photographs, contractor records, and any other requested documentation.
Complete any required final verification or inspection and remain within current rebate caps and program availability.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Marietta’s current offers are prescriptive rebates with measure-specific preverification, receipt, product, and final-verification rules rather than competitive scoring. A qualifying complete claim is likely to be approved.
reviews.evidenceText: The city’s current rebate page lists qualifying electric and water measures, product or conversion specifications, receipt uploads, and preverification or final verification for selected measures. The source record includes some broader equipment mappings not expressly supported by the current page.

approvalRequirements: Control an eligible project site in MCE’s service area and propose an eligible renewable generator with an inverter nameplate capacity from 1 to 5 megawatts.
Submit a complete Feed-In Tariff application and obtain a place in the available capacity queue under the current first-come, first-served process.
Demonstrate site control, project financing and development capability, and compliance with the tariff’s technology, pricing, storage, milestone, and commercial-operation requirements.
Obtain applicable local land-use permits, environmental review, construction permits, and a clear path to Pacific Gas and Electric interconnection.
Receive MCE application approval and execute the standardized 15-year power purchase agreement.
Complete interconnection, construction, testing, metering, commissioning, and commercial-operation milestones within the agreement schedule.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: MCE currently has a standardized, first-come Feed-In Tariff with published project and contracting conditions and remaining capacity. A complete eligible project that secures capacity and the required permits and interconnection path is likely to receive the standard power purchase agreement.
reviews.evidenceText: MCE’s current tariff page covers 1-to-5-megawatt eligible renewable projects, first-come capacity allocation, local permitting and environmental review, PG&E interconnection, project milestones, and a standardized 15-year agreement. The current tariff does not substantiate the record’s geothermal-heat-pump or solar-water-heating mappings.

approvalRequirements: Be a Marshall Municipal Utilities commercial or industrial electric customer and install the measure at an eligible account location.
Select a measure in the current Bright Energy Solutions commercial and industrial portfolio and meet its operating-hour, technical, efficiency, replacement, eligible-cost, and installation rules.
Obtain written preapproval before purchase or installation for custom projects and for any prescriptive measure that requires it.
Submit the current application with the project scope, calculations where required, paid invoices, equipment specifications, model information, contractor records, and proof of installation.
Allow preinstallation or postinstallation inspection and remain within applicable incremental-cost, project, and program caps.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current commercial portfolio combines prescriptive measures with preapproved custom projects under published technical, documentation, cost-cap, and verification rules. A conforming claim is likely to receive the calculated incentive.
reviews.evidenceText: Marshall Municipal Utilities currently offers Bright Energy Solutions incentives for lighting, HVAC and heat pumps, geothermal, motors and drives, food service, compressed air, and custom efficiency projects. Custom projects require preapproval and all claims require current project documentation.

approvalRequirements: Be a Marshall Municipal Utilities residential customer and install the measure at the qualifying service address.
Purchase and install a measure included in the current residential rebate portfolio and meet its equipment, efficiency, sizing, fuel, installation, and customer eligibility specifications.
Use the current measure-specific application and satisfy any required preapproval, contractor, recycling, connected-device, or program-enrollment condition.
Submit the application with the paid invoice, manufacturer and model information, efficiency ratings, contractor or installation records, and other required attachments by the current deadline.
Allow Marshall Municipal Utilities or Bright Energy Solutions to verify the installation before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Marshall’s current residential rebates are prescriptive and use objective customer, equipment, documentation, and verification conditions. A complete qualifying claim is likely to be paid after review.
reviews.evidenceText: The current residential page lists qualifying appliances, HVAC and heat pumps, thermostats, geothermal systems, water heating, electric vehicles, lighting, and water measures and provides measure-specific applications and specifications.

approvalRequirements: Be a Marshfield Utilities electric customer and install the system at a property receiving direct electric service from the utility.
Purchase and install a qualifying ground-source heat-pump system covered by the current utility-linked rebate application.
Complete the customer, dealer, system, model, serial-number, installation, and equipment information requested on the application.
Submit the completed application and paid receipt or invoice while the allocated rebate funds remain available.
Permit Marshfield Utilities to inspect and verify the installation before issuing the rebate.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current Marshfield Utilities page links a prescriptive ground-source heat-pump rebate that is processed first-come while funds remain. A qualifying documented installation is likely to be paid if funding is still available.
reviews.evidenceText: Marshfield Utilities’ current efficiency page links a ground-source heat-pump rebate application requiring utility service at the installation site, equipment and dealer details, a receipt, and utility inspection. The local current page does not substantiate a general air-source heat-pump or thermostat rebate under this record.

approvalRequirements: Own an eligible commercial, industrial, nonprofit, agricultural, or qualifying multifamily property in a Maryland jurisdiction participating in the statewide C-PACE structure.
Propose a qualifying energy-efficiency, renewable-energy, water, electrification, or resiliency improvement that is permanently affixed to the property.
Apply through the Maryland Clean Energy Center program process and select a willing private capital provider and qualified project team.
Submit property, title, tax, mortgage, borrower, contractor, technical, savings, cost, and financing documentation required for program review and capital-provider underwriting.
Keep taxes and mortgage obligations current and obtain required mortgage-holder, owner, tenant, governmental, and other consents.
Receive program and jurisdictional approval, execute the financing and assessment agreements, and record the assessment before closing and construction disbursement.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Maryland C-PACE is privately funded property-assessed financing, not an automatic rebate. Approval depends on property and project eligibility, private underwriting, lender consent, jurisdictional participation, negotiated terms, and closing documentation.
reviews.evidenceText: The Maryland Clean Energy Center currently administers the statewide commercial PACE platform and describes private capital, voluntary property assessments, eligible clean-energy and resilience projects, standardized review, and coordination among property owners, capital providers, contractors, lenders, and local governments.

approvalRequirements: Be a Mason County PUD 3 commercial or industrial customer and install the project at an eligible service address.
Contact the PUD conservation team before committing to the project when the measure requires eligibility screening, preinspection, custom review, or incentive reservation.
Select qualifying equipment or building-envelope work and meet the current technical, efficiency, sizing, operating, contractor, and installation requirements.
Submit the applicable application with project scope, calculations where requested, invoices, equipment specifications, model information, contractor records, and proof of installation.
Pass any required preinstallation or postinstallation inspection and remain within project caps and available conservation funds.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: PUD 3’s current commercial conservation pathway uses measure-specific eligibility, preproject contact, documentation, and verification rather than competitive scoring. A qualifying approved project is likely to receive the calculated rebate.
reviews.evidenceText: Current PUD 3 materials direct commercial customers to conservation staff for project-specific incentives and describe qualifying heat-pump, water-heating, envelope, and other efficiency measures with applications, eligibility review, and inspection or verification as applicable.

approvalRequirements: Be a Mason County PUD 3 residential customer and install the measure at the qualifying service address.
Select equipment or weatherization work included in the current residential incentive portfolio and meet its technical, efficiency, sizing, contractor, and installation requirements.
Obtain any required preapproval or preinspection before work; insulation projects require a PUD 3 preinspection to establish eligibility.
Use the applicable current application and submit paid invoices, equipment model and efficiency information, contractor records, photographs, and other required documentation.
Complete any required postinstallation inspection, connected-device enrollment, or program participation condition before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: PUD 3 publishes prescriptive residential incentives with objective customer, equipment, preinspection, documentation, and verification rules. A complete qualifying claim is likely to be approved after the required review.
reviews.evidenceText: PUD 3’s current residential materials describe heat-pump, heat-pump-water-heater, insulation, appliance, and Level 2 charging incentives. They include measure-specific applications and state that insulation must be preinspected before installation.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Massachusetts residential customer of a participating Mass Save sponsor and install the measure at a qualifying residence.
Select a measure currently offered by Mass Save and meet the applicable home type, fuel, equipment, efficiency, sizing, installation, and replacement requirements.
Complete a no-cost Home Energy Assessment, participating-contractor process, or written preauthorization when required for the measure.
Use an eligible installer or contractor and complete permitting, installation, commissioning, and any required control or program enrollment.
Submit the current rebate application with paid invoices, equipment and efficiency records, contractor documentation, and other measure-specific attachments by the deadline.
Pass any required installation verification or quality-assurance review and remain within current incentive caps and available funds.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Mass Save’s current residential offers are generally prescriptive and use published customer, assessment, contractor, technical, documentation, and verification rules. A qualifying complete claim is likely to receive the stated incentive, subject to caps and funds.
reviews.evidenceText: Mass Save’s current residential pages organize incentives for home assessments, weatherization, heating and cooling, water heating, appliances and products, electric vehicles, and related measures and identify measure-specific assessment, contractor, application, and verification steps.

approvalRequirements: Own an eligible Massachusetts residence and be a customer of a participating Mass Save sponsor.
Select an improvement currently eligible for Mass Save financing and complete a Home Energy Assessment when required for that measure.
Obtain a proposal from a participating or otherwise eligible contractor and secure Mass Save project authorization before beginning the financed work.
Apply through a participating lender and provide the borrower, credit, income, property, mortgage, contractor, project, and cost information required for underwriting.
Pass the lender’s credit and repayment review and execute the loan documents before funding.
Complete the approved work, sign the completion documents, submit invoices and rebate records, and pass any required Mass Save verification before final disbursement.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The HEAT Loan combines Mass Save project eligibility with independent participating-lender underwriting. Even an authorized efficiency project is not guaranteed financing until the homeowner passes credit review and closes the loan.
reviews.evidenceText: Mass Save currently describes zero-interest financing for qualifying weatherization, heat pumps, heat-pump water heaters, batteries, windows with weatherization, and related work. The process requires project authorization and then participating-lender approval, completion, and verification.

approvalRequirements: Be a business customer of a participating Mass Save sponsor and meet the current small-business annual energy-use thresholds.
Submit the program interest or eligibility form and provide utility-account, facility, operating, and contact information.
Complete the no-cost small-business energy assessment and receive a project proposal identifying eligible measures and the sponsor contribution.
Accept the proposal and use the assigned qualified vendor or an approved customer-directed installation pathway before purchasing or installing covered measures.
Complete the approved installation and provide invoices, equipment records, permits, and other closeout documentation requested by the sponsor.
Pass postinstallation verification and pay the customer share of project cost before the sponsor incentive is applied.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current Small Business pathway provides a defined no-cost assessment and prescriptive project proposal rather than competitive grant scoring. An eligible business that accepts and completes the approved proposal is likely to receive the sponsor contribution.
reviews.evidenceText: Mass Save currently defines small-business eligibility by annual electricity or gas use, offers a no-cost assessment, and provides qualified-vendor or customer-directed installation options with sponsor support for approved lighting, HVAC, weatherization, and other measures.

approvalRequirements: Be a commercial or industrial customer of a participating Mass Save electric sponsor with a building suitable for a deep energy retrofit.
Contact the electric sponsor and complete initial feasibility screening and a no-cost assessment or scoping process.
Develop an acceptable integrated retrofit roadmap designed to achieve the program’s target greenhouse-gas reduction and identify the required measures, costs, schedule, and verification plan.
Obtain sponsor acceptance of the roadmap and any project-specific incentive, technical-assistance, commissioning, or verification commitments before implementation.
Implement the approved retrofit measures, complete commissioning and corrective work, and document installed scope, costs, energy performance, and greenhouse-gas results.
Meet the applicable performance milestone and pass sponsor measurement, verification, and closeout review before receiving performance-based or technical-assistance payments.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Deep Energy Retrofit support depends on building feasibility, sponsor acceptance of an integrated roadmap, substantial greenhouse-gas performance, project delivery, and verified results. Baseline customer eligibility therefore does not assure an award.
reviews.evidenceText: Mass Save’s current Deep Energy Retrofit offering targets major greenhouse-gas reduction, begins with sponsor contact and no-cost scoping, and supports roadmap development, implementation, commissioning, and verification. Retro-commissioning is one project component rather than a stand-alone automatic rebate.
